text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired — service=hosted-inference, policy=primary-secondary-manager, incident=PD-211234. Trigger: 5xx spike in region us-west. Threshold: 8% error rate over 2 minutes.
jamie: I’m on pager. looking at logs now.
pagerduty-bot: PD Notification: page sent to primary on-call (jamie).
jamie: ack'ing the page.
jamie: ack — taking ownership. quick check: are we seeing increased tail latencies too or just 5xx?
alex: I can pull env logs, hang on.
sanjay: pinging the console — seeing a surge of 502/503 from our edge -> inference frontends.
jamie: copying runbook section: "hosted-inference 5xx spike". first step is to confirm worker pool health and queue depth.
incident-bot: Runbook link: https://confluence.redwood/runbooks/hosted-inference-5xx (attached)
jamie: running: kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide | grep worker
jamie: result: several worker-* pods in CrashLoopBackOff in us-west-1a.
alex: grabbing pod logs from worker-7d9f
alex: logs show repeated OOMKilled with rapid memory growth after input batching spikes. stacktrace shows C++ inference runtime OOM at kvcache.cpp:312
jamie: can we temporarily reduce max_batch_size? if batching config spiked it could blow memory.
sanjay: can toggle batching via config flag in config service. pushing change to reduce max_batch_size from 64 -> 16 for us-west.
lina: FYI support queue: customers are opening cases about 503s. I posted a status update to the status page draft.
pagerduty-bot: PD Notification: primary did not acknowledge within 5m. Escalating to secondary (alex).
alex: ack — stepping in as secondary. switching traffic to dedicated pool fallback for prod customers in us-west.
jamie: thanks. can you spin up the fallback route? command: infra-cli reroute --service hosted-inference --region us-west --target dedicated-pool-3 --dry-run false
alex: started reroute, shifting ~30% traffic immediately, will ramp to 100% in 2m if stable.
marie: pinging manager — overlay question: any customer SLAs hit?
lina: initial impact estimate: ~12% of production requests failing in us-west over last 3m, affecting ~90 tenants (mostly small). No enterprise customers on dedicated capacity flagged yet.
jamie: will open bridge: zoom/bridge link https://zoom.redwood/bridges/PD-211234
jamie: running quick health checks: 
```
# curl check to inference front door
for h in api-us-west{1,2}.redwood.internal; do curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" http://$h/health || echo fail:$h; done
```
alex: health shows api-us-west1 -> 503, api-us-west2 -> 200. Likely partial AZ issue.
sanjay: investigating autoscaler logs — new workers failed to provision in us-west-1a due to node image mismatch (kubelet couldn't pull optimized runtime image).
jamie: interesting — that explains CrashLoop + OOM noise if older image had a memory leak. can we force new nodes in us-west-1b?
alex: yes, spinning up nodes in 1b and scaling dedicated-pool-3. provisioning now (~90s).
marie: marked incident severity P1. Noted to execs.
incident-bot: PagerDuty update: PD-211234 escalated to manager (marie) due to secondary ack within escalation window.
marie: on the bridge. thanks all. priority now: stabilize customer traffic, mitigate impact, and identify root cause for bad node images.
lina: posted interim status: "We are investigating increased 503 errors in us-west. Some customers may experience degraded inference performance. Engineers are working on a mitigation. Updates every 15 minutes." :hourglass:
jamie: reroute finished: ramp to 100%. monitoring latency and error rate.
alex: metrics: error rate dropped from 12% -> 1.8% in the next 90s after reroute. latency stable.
sanjay: new nodes came up in 1b and joined the pool; worker pods now starting healthy images.
jamie: rolling restart of workers in us-west-1a to ensure they pick the correct image: kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-worker -n inference --field-selector='spec.nodeName!=deprecated-node'
alex: restarting; watching pod readiness.
marie: good call. can we schedule a postmortem? assign owner?
jamie: I'll own the postmortem. timeline + impact + remediation.
lina: support will send an outreach to affected tenants with credits. drafting email now.
pagerduty-bot: PD Notification: incident PD-211234 acknowledged by jamie, escalated to alex, manager marie on call.
incident-bot: Note: created incident ticket INC-5598 in our tracker with initial notes and action items.
jamie: observed a few residual 502s during restart window but overall healthy. will keep monitoring for 30m.
alex: pulling kubelet event logs — found image tag mismatch: infra-proxy:1.5.0 vs expected infra-proxy:1.6.0 on deprecated node images. placing a node group cordon for cleanup.
sanjay: filing infra change request to prevent automated deploys to older nodegroup without compatible images.
marie: adding follow-ups: (1) pin autoscaler to avoid provisioning deprecated nodegroups, (2) add batching safety limits to runtime config, (3) add alert for node image mismatch.
jamie: marking incident as mitigated at 4123457120 — error rate <2%, customer impact substantially reduced.
lina: updating status page: "Mitigation in progress. Traffic rerouted and systems recovering. Investigating root cause. Next update in 30 minutes."
marie: thanks team. keep the bridge open for 30m monitoring then we can close.
jamie: closing bridge at 4123457200, creating follow-up tickets: PM-502 (postmortem), INFRA-847 (nodegroup fix), RUNTIME-329 (batching guardrails).
incident-bot: Incident PD-211234 status: Mitigated. Follow-ups created.
sanjay: noted. will join postmortem.
alex: nice work. :white_check_mark:
lina: support follow-ups queued.
jamie: final note: primary oncall got the initial page and acked but escalation timing still valid — we'll adjust PD timeout to 4m for this policy so secondary gets less noisy pages. filing PD policy tweak in INFOPS-120.
marie: agreed. thanks everyone.
